html:
SMTO-OUT-0001 — This Task has too many steps for SMTO to read back at once

GUID: 3ca14434-e2aa-4d3f-8608-8adcb01ac818
Slug: receipt-extraction-limit
Domain: OUT · Subsystem: out

What happened

  • This Task recorded more steps or more data than SMTO reads back in one go (over 512 steps or about 4 MB). The Task's results weren't changed; only this action couldn't use them.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were saving steps from this Task for reuse, try it on a shorter Task that does only the part you want to keep. SMTO reuses steps only when it can read the whole Task, and shorter Tasks fit within the limit.
  2. Use the files, reports or other results this Task already produced instead of running it again. Running it again would repeat its actions and record just as many steps.
  3. For future large jobs, ask the Agent to save big results to files and reply with a short summary. Results kept in files add far less to what SMTO has to read back.

What success looks like

  • The action works on the shorter Task, or you have what you need from the existing results.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the Task's history to get under the limit; it's the record of what actually ran.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • RunStore.ordered_receipts stopped because the run's receipts exceed the extraction limit (512 receipts or 4 MiB of combined arguments, results and exact artifacts), and no partial receipt list is returned.

What this means

  • Ordered receipt extraction reaches its configured receipt-count or combined argument/result/artifact byte bound before producing the requested exact set. Output extraction, rendering and summaries do not own execution truth. Their failure cannot turn a completed operation into unexecuted work or justify replay; retained exact receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Ordered receipt extraction reaches its configured receipt-count or combined argument/result/artifact byte bound before producing the requested exact set.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the extraction count/byte limit and existing operation/artifact references; missing extraction is not missing execution.

How to fix it

  • Use a smaller run or an existing retained artifact or file reference for the needed evidence; the bound is the limit/max_bytes defaults of RunStore.ordered_receipts used by callers such as execution_cache.management, recipes.recorder and parameters.mappings. Exact execution receipts remain the source of truth; do not rerun the operation to reduce this read.
  • Select a smaller supported portion or use an existing retained artifact/file reference. Exact execution receipts remain the source of truth; do not rerun the operation to reduce this read.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported smaller read or retained artifact supplies the exact needed evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • Output extraction, rendering and summaries do not own execution truth. Their failure cannot turn a completed operation into unexecuted work or justify replay; retained exact receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
